from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching data for section_1
        title_text = "The Mystery of Chaos"
        lecture_lines = [
            "The world is often messy and unpredictable.",
            "Individual data points can appear completely random.",
            "Can we find order within this chaotic data?"
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Visual styling
        self.title.set_color("#ADD8E6") # Light blue as per storyboard
        YELLOW_HEX = "#FFFF00"
        RED_HEX = "#FF0000"
        GREEN_HEX = "#00FF00"
        WHITE_HEX = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a chaotic scatter plot of dots with random sizes in yellow.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW_HEX))
        
        dots = VGroup()
        np.random.seed(42)
        # Use grid area B1 to E6 for the chaotic dots
        tl = self.grid["B1"]
        br = self.grid["E6"]
        
        for _ in range(40):
            rand_x = np.random.uniform(tl[0], br[0])
            rand_y = np.random.uniform(br[1], tl[1])
            dot = Dot(
                point=[rand_x, rand_y, 0], 
                radius=np.random.uniform(0.04, 0.12), 
                color=YELLOW_HEX
            )
            dots.add(dot)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(dots))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Flash extreme dots in red to show data variability.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED_HEX))
        
        # Select the most "extreme" dots based on their size
        sorted_dots = sorted(dots, key=lambda d: d.radius)
        extreme_dots = VGroup(sorted_dots[0], sorted_dots[1], sorted_dots[-1], sorted_dots[-2])
        
        # Flashing red to highlight variability
        self.play(*[Flash(d, color=RED_HEX, flash_radius=0.3) for d in extreme_dots])
        self.play(extreme_dots.animate.set_color(RED_HEX), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(extreme_dots.animate.set_color(YELLOW_HEX), run_time=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show a white pulsing question mark in the center of the chaos.
        # Transition dots into a skewed green population bar chart.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN_HEX))
        
        question_mark = Text("?", font_size=80, color=WHITE_HEX)
        self.place_in_area(question_mark, "C3", "D4")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(question_mark))
        self.play(question_mark.animate.scale(1.2), rate_func=there_and_back, run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Create a skewed green bar chart
        bar_heights = [0.5, 1.2, 3.2, 2.0, 1.0, 0.6]
        bars = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(
                height=h, 
                width=0.6, 
                fill_opacity=0.8, 
                fill_color=GREEN_HEX, 
                stroke_color=GREEN_HEX
            ) for h in bar_heights
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15, aligned_edge=DOWN)
        
        self.place_in_area(bars, "B1", "E6")
        
        # Organize dots into groups to transform into bars smoothly
        dot_groups = [VGroup() for _ in range(len(bars))]
        for i, dot in enumerate(dots):
            dot_groups[i % len(bars)].add(dot)
            
        self.play(
            FadeOut(question_mark),
            *[ReplacementTransform(dg, bar) for dg, bar in zip(dot_groups, bars)]
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # COLORS
        ORANGE_COLOR = "#FFA500"
        MAGENTA_COLOR = "#FF00FF"
        CYAN_COLOR = "#00FFFF"

        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite: The Building Blocks",
            [
                "Every population has a mean and standard deviation.",
                "A distribution shows how often different values occur.",
                "Our \"Chaos Island\" monsters have a flat distribution."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color the lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(ORANGE_COLOR))

        # Setup Axes for the background
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 100, 20],
            y_range=[0, 1, 0.5],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "font_size": 18}
        ).set_color(GRAY)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E6")
        
        # Mean Line (mu)
        mu_val = 50
        mu_line = Line(
            axes.c2p(mu_val, 0),
            axes.c2p(mu_val, 0.8),
            color=ORANGE_COLOR
        )
        mu_label = MathTex(r"\mu", color=ORANGE_COLOR, font_size=24)
        mu_label.next_to(mu_line, UP, buff=0.1)

        # Standard Deviation (sigma) - Represented by arrows
        sigma_val = 20
        sigma_arrow = DoubleArrow(
            axes.c2p(mu_val - sigma_val, 0.4),
            axes.c2p(mu_val + sigma_val, 0.4),
            color=MAGENTA_COLOR,
            buff=0,
            tip_length=0.15
        )
        sigma_label = MathTex(r"\sigma", color=MAGENTA_COLOR, font_size=24)
        sigma_label.next_to(sigma_arrow, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(Create(mu_line), Write(mu_label))
        self.play(Create(sigma_arrow), Write(sigma_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Color the lecture line
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(CYAN_COLOR)
        )

        # Distribution Chart - A flat rectangular graph
        # We represent "how often different values occur" by filling the probability area
        uniform_rect = Rectangle(
            width=axes.x_axis.get_length(),
            height=axes.y_axis.get_unit_size() * 0.5,
            fill_color=CYAN_COLOR,
            fill_opacity=0.3,
            stroke_color=CYAN_COLOR
        )
        # Position rectangle centered in the axes area for uniform distribution
        uniform_rect.move_to(axes.c2p(50, 0.25))

        self.play(FadeIn(uniform_rect))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Color the lecture line
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(CYAN_COLOR)
        )

        # Emphasize the "flat" nature
        # We can highlight the top edge of the rectangle
        flat_top = Line(
            axes.c2p(0, 0.5),
            axes.c2p(100, 0.5),
            color=CYAN_COLOR,
            stroke_width=6
        )

        self.play(Create(flat_top))
        self.play(Flash(flat_top, color=CYAN_COLOR, line_length=0.3))
        self.wait(2)

        # Cleanup for next section if needed
        self.play(FadeOut(flat_top), FadeOut(uniform_rect), FadeOut(axes), FadeOut(mu_line), FadeOut(mu_label), FadeOut(sigma_arrow), FadeOut(sigma_label))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title_text = "The Sampling Experiment"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Let's take random groups, or samples, of monsters.",
            "For each group, we calculate the average weight.",
            "This average is called the \"Sample Mean.\"",
            "We repeat this process many, many times.",
            "Each sample gives us one new data point."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors defined in storyboard
        LIME = "#32CD32"
        GOLD = "#FFD700"
        WHITE_CLR = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Let's take random groups, or samples, of monsters."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(LIME))
        
        # Create monster icons (small squares with eyes)
        monsters = VGroup(*[
            VGroup(
                Square(side_length=0.15, color=LIME, fill_opacity=1),
                Dot(radius=0.02, color=BLACK).shift(UP*0.03 + LEFT*0.03),
                Dot(radius=0.02, color=BLACK).shift(UP*0.03 + RIGHT*0.03)
            ) for _ in range(30)
        ])
        monsters.arrange_in_grid(rows=5, cols=6, buff=0.15)
        self.place_in_area(monsters, "B1", "E3", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(monsters))
        # Flickering effect (simulation of sampling)
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(*[
                Indicate(m, color=LIME, scale_factor=1.2) 
                for m in monsters
            ], lag_ratio=0.05),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "For each group, we calculate the average weight."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GOLD)
        )
        
        formula = MathTex(r"\bar{X} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} X_i", color=GOLD)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A2", "A5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "This average is called the \"Sample Mean.\""
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GOLD)
        )
        
        label = Text("Sample Mean", font_size=24, color=GOLD)
        label.next_to(formula, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "We repeat this process many, many times."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE_CLR)
        )
        
        # Populate a white list with multiple sample mean values
        means_list = VGroup(*[
            MathTex(fr"\bar{{X}}_{{{i+1}}}", color=WHITE_CLR) 
            for i in range(5)
        ]).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(means_list, "B5", "E6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Sampling animation loop showing new data points appearing
        for i in range(5):
            # Highlight a "random" subset of monsters to represent a new sample
            indices = np.random.choice(range(30), 10, replace=False)
            subset = VGroup(*[monsters[idx] for idx in indices])
            
            self.play(
                subset.animate.set_color(GOLD),
                run_time=0.3
            )
            self.play(
                FadeIn(means_list[i]),
                subset.animate.set_color(LIME),
                run_time=0.3
            )
            
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "Each sample gives us one new data point."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE_CLR)
        )
        
        self.play(Indicate(means_list, color=WHITE_CLR))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Visual Transformation"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Watch the distribution of these sample means change.",
            "Initially, the averages might look a bit scattered.",
            "As we collect more samples, a pattern emerges.",
            "The messy distribution morphs into a smooth curve.",
            "It becomes the famous, symmetrical Bell Curve."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show the original messy rectangular histogram dimmed in the background.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Creating a placeholder "messy" histogram using bars
        heights = [1.2, 0.8, 1.5, 0.5, 1.1, 1.4, 0.7, 1.3]
        bars = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=0.4, height=h, fill_opacity=0.3, color=GRAY, stroke_width=1) for h in heights])
        bars.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1, aligned_edge=DOWN)
        self.place_in_area(bars, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Add a baseline
        baseline = Line(bars.get_left(), bars.get_right(), color=WHITE).shift(DOWN * 0.05)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(bars), Create(baseline))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Plot new sample mean points in yellow (#FFFF00) along the horizontal axis.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        np.random.seed(42)
        num_dots = 30
        dots = VGroup()
        center_x = bars.get_center()[0]
        base_y = baseline.get_y() + 0.1
        
        # Generate random positions clustered in the middle
        for _ in range(num_dots):
            # Cluster around center_x
            x_offset = np.random.normal(0, 0.8) 
            dot = Dot(point=[center_x + x_offset, base_y, 0], radius=0.06, color="#FFFF00")
            dots.add(dot)

        self.play(Create(dots), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Morph the accumulating points into a rough light blue (#ADD8E6) bell shape.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a rough bell shape using points
        # Coordinates are relative to the center of the area
        rough_points = [
            [-2.0, 0.0, 0], [-1.5, 0.4, 0], [-1.0, 1.2, 0], [-0.5, 2.0, 0], 
            [0.0, 2.5, 0], [0.5, 1.9, 0], [1.0, 1.3, 0], [1.5, 0.5, 0], [2.0, 0.0, 0]
        ]
        rough_curve = VMobject(color="#ADD8E6", stroke_width=4)
        rough_curve.set_points_as_corners([np.array(p) for p in rough_points])
        
        # Position rough_curve in the same area
        self.place_in_area(rough_curve, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.7)
        rough_curve.align_to(baseline, DOWN)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(dots),
            FadeOut(bars),
            Create(rough_curve),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Smooth the rough shape into a perfect pink (#FFC0CB) normal distribution curve.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Use an Axes to generate the smooth curve (axes won't be added to scene)
        ax = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3], 
            y_range=[0, 0.5], 
            x_length=5, 
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        )
        self.place_in_area(ax, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        smooth_curve = ax.plot(
            lambda x: 0.4 * np.exp(-0.5 * x**2),
            color="#FFC0CB",
            stroke_width=5
        )
        # Ensure it aligns with the baseline for consistency
        smooth_curve.align_to(baseline, DOWN)

        self.play(
            Transform(rough_curve, smooth_curve),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Flash the final curve to emphasize the completed transformation.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(
            Indicate(rough_curve, color="#FFC0CB", scale_factor=1.2),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Core Theorem (The Magic Rule)"
        lines = [
            "This is the Central Limit Theorem in action.",
            "The center stays at the true population mean.",
            "Increasing sample size makes the curve much narrower.",
            "With enough samples, the shape is always Normal.",
            "Chaos transforms into predictable, mathematical order."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        GREEN = "#00FF00"
        RED = "#FF0000"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the formula X-bar ~ N(mu, sigma squared over n)
        formula = MathTex(r"\bar{X} \sim N\left(\mu, \frac{\sigma^2}{n}\right)", color=WHITE_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A2", "A5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Write(formula), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight the constant center line mu in red (#FF0000)
        # Position the center in the grid area C2-F5
        center_x = (self.grid["C1"][0] + self.grid["C6"][0]) / 2
        center_y_base = self.grid["F3"][1]
        center_y_top = self.grid["C3"][1]
        
        mean_line = Line(
            start=[center_x, center_y_base, 0],
            end=[center_x, center_y_top + 0.5, 0],
            color=RED,
            stroke_width=2
        )
        mu_label = MathTex(r"\mu", color=RED).scale(0.8)
        mu_label.next_to(mean_line, UP, buff=0.1)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(mean_line), Write(mu_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Draw a wide green (#00FF00) bell curve representing a small sample size.
        # Use ValueTracker for n to animate the narrowing
        n_tracker = ValueTracker(1)
        sigma_base = 1.0 # Base width for visual representation
        
        def get_bell_curve():
            n_val = n_tracker.get_value()
            curr_sigma = sigma_base / np.sqrt(n_val)
            # Amplitude adjustment: height proportional to sqrt(n)
            # We add a base height so it doesn't vanish and scale it for the grid
            height_scale = 0.4 * np.sqrt(n_val) 
            
            # Using ParametricFunction with small t_range for performance
            curve = ParametricFunction(
                lambda t: np.array([
                    center_x + t, 
                    center_y_base + height_scale * np.exp(-0.5 * (t / curr_sigma)**2), 
                    0
                ]),
                t_range=[-2.5, 2.5],
                color=GREEN
            )
            return curve

        bell_curve = always_redraw(get_bell_curve)
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(bell_curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

        # Squeeze the green bell curve to make it taller and narrower.
        n_text_label = Text("n = ", font_size=24)
        n_value = DecimalNumber(1, num_decimal_places=0, font_size=24)
        n_group = VGroup(n_text_label, n_value).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(n_group, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Update DecimalNumber based on ValueTracker
        n_value.add_updater(lambda d: d.set_value(n_tracker.get_value()))
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(n_group)
        self.play(n_tracker.animate.set_value(30), run_time=5, rate_func=smooth)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Chaos transforms into predictable, mathematical order.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Final highlight on the result
        box = SurroundingRectangle(formula, color=YELLOW, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(box))
        self.wait(2)

        # Final cleanup for color
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

outline.topic: The Magic of the Central Limit Theorem: Finding Order in Chaos
outline.target_audience: University students or high school students with basic statistics knowledge

sections.title: The Mystery of Chaos
sections.content: Introduce the idea that the world is messy and unpredictable. Define the goal: How do we find a predictable pattern when the underlying data is completely random or skewed?
sections.example: Imagine 'Chaos Island' inhabited by various monsters. Their weights are totally random—some weigh 1kg, some weigh 500kg. There is no 'normal' shape to their population distribution.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Building Blocks
sections.content: Briefly review 'Population Mean' (μ) and 'Standard Deviation' (σ). Explain that a 'Distribution' is just a map showing how often different values occur. Use a visual bar chart showing a non-normal (e.g., flat or bimodal) distribution.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Uniform Distribution' where every monster weight from 1 to 100 has an equal chance of appearing, represented by a flat rectangular graph.

sections.title: The Sampling Experiment
sections.content: Introduce the core mechanism: Sampling. Instead of looking at individual monsters, we take groups (samples) of size 'n'. Calculate the average weight of each group. This is the 'Sample Mean'.
sections.example: Professor Owl takes 30 monsters at random, calculates their average weight, and writes it down. He repeats this process 1,000 times, creating a list of 1,000 different average weights.

sections.title: The Visual Transformation
sections.content: Animate the 'Distribution of Sample Means'. As more samples are collected, the histogram of those averages begins to shift and morph. Regardless of the original 'Chaos Island' shape, the new graph of averages starts to look like a Bell Curve.
sections.example: Watch a digital histogram where the messy rectangular bars of individual weights gradually transform into a smooth, symmetrical 'Normal Distribution' curve as the number of samples increases.

sections.title: The Core Theorem (The Magic Rule)
sections.content: State the Central Limit Theorem formally but visually: 1. The mean of the sample means equals the population mean. 2. The spread (standard error) gets narrower as sample size 'n' increases. 3. The shape becomes Normal if 'n' is large enough (usually n ≥ 30).
sections.example: Show a mathematical formula: X̄ ~ N(μ, σ²/n). Use an animation where increasing 'n' (the group size) physically squeezes the bell curve to make it taller and thinner (more precise).

sections.title: Real-World Application
sections.content: Explain why this is the 'Fundamental Theorem of Statistics'. It allows us to make precise predictions about a whole population even if we only have a few samples, because we know the averages will always follow the Bell Curve.
sections.example: A factory wants to ensure the average battery life of 1 million units is 100 hours. By testing 50 groups of 30 batteries, they can use the CLT to calculate exactly how confident they are in the quality of the entire million-unit batch.
